title: Quasi-compact separated direct image preserves quasi-coherence on spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with these properties as defined in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. For any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], its module direct image $f_*F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$ is quasi-coherent. Here $f_*$ denotes direct image for the morphism of ringed small etale topoi induced by $f$, with the scalar action from $\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), restricted to separated morphisms; separated implies quasi-separated since a closed immersion is quasi-compact. Ringed direct image is spaces-properties.tex equation-push-pull preceding Tag 03LV.

proof.text: Let V -> Y be any affine scheme etale morphism, and choose a surjective etale map W -> Y from a scheme W, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The family {V -> Y, W -> Y} consists of etale maps from schemes and is jointly surjective because W -> Y already is. Applying the forward implication of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] to this family shows that f_V:X_V=X\times_YV -> V is quasi-compact and separated. By [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] (with Y'=V), the restriction of f_*F to V is canonically (f_V)_*(F|_{X_V}). Since quasi-coherence is the local presentation condition of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and every object of Y_et is covered by affine etale schemes (Zariski affine opens of a scheme etale over Y), a local presentation of the restriction to each affine V, composed with the covering of an object by such V, is a local presentation on Y_et; so it is enough to prove this restricted module quasi-coherent on V_et for every such V.

source.place: Tag 03M9, first proof paragraph: affine etale test V, base change f', and the reduction to an affine target; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX for the module restriction formula.

proof.text: Fix V and abbreviate X_V and f_V by X and f, so that V is affine. Quasi-compactness of f gives a quasi-compact scheme atlas over X; refining by a finite affine cover and taking its finite disjoint union gives a surjective etale map p:U -> X from an affine scheme. Put R=U\times_XU. The fibre-product and etale-cover statement [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes R a scheme, and the atlas equalizer lemma [lem-trf-space-pushforward-atlas-equalizer] identifies f_*F with the kernel of a_*F_U -> b_*F_R, the difference of the two projection restrictions, where a=f\circ p and b:R->V is either composite.

source.place: Tag 03M9, affine-target paragraph: choose an affine surjective etale U -> X and apply Tag 03M8; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03E3 for the quasi-compact atlas.

proof.text: The map R -> U\times_VU is the base change of the representable diagonal X -> X\times_VX along U\times_VU -> X\times_VX: indeed R=U\times_XU = X\times_{X\times_VX}(U\times_VU). Since f is separated, that diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test, and U\times_VU is a scheme test, so R -> U\times_VU is a closed immersion of schemes (equivalently, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] applied to the scheme test). The target U\times_VU is affine because U and V are, and a closed subscheme of an affine scheme is affine, so R is affine. Consequently a:U->V and b:R->V are morphisms between affine schemes, hence quasi-compact and separated (their diagonals are the closed immersions given by the surjective multiplication maps). Restriction of the local quasi-coherent presentation of F to the localized etale sites of the charts U and R remains such a presentation, so F_U and F_R are quasi-coherent, by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and the restriction description in [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction].

source.place: Tag 03M9, affine-target paragraph: quasi-separatedness makes R -> U x_Y U quasi-compact and separated, so a and b are qcqs scheme morphisms.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] on the affine schemes U and R and on the affine target V. The quasi-coherent restrictions F_U and F_R are, by essential surjectivity, isomorphic to (H_U)_et and (H_R)_et for quasi-coherent Zariski modules H_U and H_R. Since a and b are quasi-compact and separated scheme morphisms (Step 3), the same node gives quasi-coherent Zariski direct images a_*H_U and b_*H_R and canonical isomorphisms (a_*H_U)_et = a_*F_U and (b_*H_R)_et = b_*F_R; in particular a_*F_U and b_*F_R are quasi-coherent modules on V_et. The difference map a_*F_U -> b_*F_R of Step 2 is therefore a morphism of O_V-modules on V_et between quasi-coherent modules, and its kernel in the module category is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-etale-quasi-coherent-kernel]. By the exact sequence of [lem-trf-space-pushforward-atlas-equalizer], f_*F is that kernel, so f_*F is quasi-coherent on V_et. Since this holds for every affine etale V -> Y, Step 1 proves that f_*F is quasi-coherent on Y_et, with its O_Y scalar action the one of the ringed direct image.

source.place: Tag 03M9, final affine-target paragraph: a_*(F|_U), b_*(F|_R) quasi-coherent by Descent 03LC, then f_*F is a kernel of quasi-coherent modules, Properties of Spaces Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent) (3), whose scheme case is Descent Tag 0GNB (3).

proof_origin.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), proof, with Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), Tag 03LX (module etale base change), Descent Tag 03LC, and Descent Tag 0GNB (3) for kernels of quasi-coherent etale modules.

from.place: Stacks spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M9, proof: reduction to affine etale tests, the affine-target atlas/equalizer argument, and scheme qcqs pushforward plus kernel closure.

split_report.summary: Split the Stacks Tag 03M9 proof into affine etale localization, the affine-atlas Cech kernel computation, the geometry making the two scheme maps qcqs, and the final scheme pushforward/kernel argument. Added one statement-only helper for Tag 03M8's atlas equalizer; all other inputs are existing DAG nodes. The separated hypothesis supplies quasi-separatedness through the closed representable diagonal, so the item statement is unchanged. Maintainer reader fix (2026-10-18): Step 1 now uses the family {V, atlas W} of etale maps from schemes (the identity of Y is not a map from a scheme); Steps 3-4 record that a and b are maps of affine schemes hence separated as the equivalence node requires; and the kernel step cites the new statement-only node lem-trf-scheme-etale-quasi-coherent-kernel (Descent 0GNB (3)) instead of the Zariski kernel lemma, whose application to etale modules needed the exactness of F -> F_et.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes Tag 03M9's three proof paragraphs below the historical lem-trf-local-term-locality ancestry: affine etale reduction; affine atlas and equalizer; qcqs scheme pushforward and kernel closure.
